correctness.rationale: Commuting Fourier Hamiltonians have exact eigenfrequencies; the symmetric two-state telegraph characteristic function solves q''+2 lambda q'+b^2 q=0 with stationary initial derivatives, yielding an exact all-time probability formula. The sine-equality congruence has solutions off the diagonal precisely for even N; their protected Fourier contributions yield the oscillatory and pi/2 mod-four alternatives. For odd N, an exactly attainable discrete sine gap gives the sharp decay exponent; positivity of leading mode coefficients and a nonzero trigonometric polynomial prove the limsup lower bound, including over/critical/under-damped cases. Rationalizing the square root gives \(N^{-4}\). Dense stochastic-Liouvillian numerical comparisons and arithmetic checks independently corroborate formulas but finite tests are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Spatially perfectly shared phase noise is a physically natural correlated-field alternative to independent local dephasing. The theorem identifies exactly when coherent modes survive (even ring parity), distinguishes undamped oscillation from static nonuniform limit at a precise phase, and derives an unexpectedly quartic long-time finite-size decay exponent for odd rings with an explicit universal coefficient. This is a structural, parameter-uniform limitation on noise-induced mixing, not a trivial finite case or mere numerical benchmark. It does not claim a proven N^4 finite-precision mixing time.
